content.text: Investigation complete. Section 24 delivers the full preferred checklist, and no other clause creates a back-door change-of-control right for the Vendor.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
input.rationale: Section 24 satisfies the preferred position in full, so no redline is warranted. 24.1 gives us a consent-free assignment right to an Affiliate and to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets (with prompt written notice only). 24.2 binds the Vendor asymmetrically in our favour: it may not assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent, with the reasonableness standard limited to assignees of adequate capability and financial standing, and it may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without our consent. 24.4 squarely closes the walk-away risk by confirming our change of control gives the Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service, and obliges cooperation with administrative changes for a permitted successor. 24.3 supplies the residual mutual consent gate at a not-unreasonably-withheld/conditioned/delayed standard, and 13.3 lets our licence rights travel with a permitted assignment. Two immaterial points short of ideal preferred wording, noted but not flagged: the competitor bar is qualified by "direct" and is subject to our own consent (a gate we control, so it operates in our favour), and 24.2's reasonableness standard is framed around assignee capability. Section 9.2's insolvency termination right is mutual, is not a change-of-control trigger, and expressly excludes a lawful reorganization that does not impair performance, so it does not undercut 24.4.
